Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: OTR launched online platforms and e-services; combined with references to online motor vehicle tax payments and digitalized processes, this indicates partial digital revenue collection rather than complete digitization across all revenue streams.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. OTR's e-services portal (télédéclaration et télépaiement, live since May 2016) enables online filing and payment of VAT, income tax (IB) and instalments; IB Bank's e-Paiement service lets taxpayers pay OTR taxes, customs-linked SEGUCE fees and port charges online; motor-vehicle tax (TVM) is also payable online; Gest-exo (2025) digitises customs exemption requests. Coverage is broad but not shown to extend to all revenue types (e.g. property tax), so Partial (2) is retained.

Comments: Evidence of specific tax e-services portals includes OTR’s Gest‑exo platform (online submission/processing of tax exemptions/waivers) becoming mandatory from Jan 1, 2026, demonstrating existence of a government tax-related online portal.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and strengthened. OTR's e-services portal (e-services.otr.tg) has offered online tax filing plus payment since May 2016, and OTR now publishes statistics on 'Télédéclaration et Télépaiement'; the 2025 Gest-exo platform adds online exemption/waiver processing. Yes (4) is now supported by a primary OTR source rather than a single news article.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: PI‑PSI/PI‑SPI enables instant transfers between banks and other financial institutions; this infrastructure supports business payments (including supplier/enterprise transfers) over bank accounts, implying B2B capability via participating banks.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with corroboration: PI-SPI (launched Sept 2025; six Togolese banks/PSPs authorised by Feb 2026) enables instant transfers between bank and business accounts across UEMOA. No source explicitly labels a distinct 'B2B' use case, so the Yes (2) rating still rests on inference from general account-to-account functionality — recommend human review to confirm a dedicated B2B/SME use case.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: World Bank case study documents NOVISSI as a fully digital end-to-end government-to-person cash transfer program in Togo, paying benefits into beneficiaries’ mobile money accounts (with MNOs auto-creating accounts when needed).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and freshened. The original Novissi programme (2020-23) was a fully digital G2P scheme paying via mobile money. A second phase, Novissi 2, launched 18 December 2025 and was rolling out nationally by January 2026, targeting up to ~700,000 beneficiaries with unconditional transfers paid via Yas/Moov mobile money. Yes - Active Use (3) remains correct.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: BCEAO states it is responsible for management (including operational and technical management) of WAEMU payment systems (SICA‑UEMOA and STAR‑UEMOA) under Regulation No. 15/2002/CM/WAMU, showing direct operation of core payment infrastructure for WAEMU member states including Togo.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a stronger, dated source. BCEAO's regulation (Art. 3, Regulation 15/2002/CM/WAMU) and its 2022-23 payment-infrastructure report confirm BCEAO directly operates SICA-UEMOA, STAR-UEMOA and SAGETIL-UMOA, and BCEAO itself launched and operates the new PI-SPI instant-payment platform. Direct Operation (5) confirmed.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Togo is aligning with WAEMU’s consumer protection directive (June 2023) aimed at strengthening consumer rights (information, quality, dispute resolution). This provides a partial consumer protection framework relevant to payment services, but sources reviewed did not confirm payment-specific protections for digital payments.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial. Togo is implementing the June 2023 WAEMU consumer-protection directive (general, cross-sector), and BCEAO's Instruction 001-01-2024 on payment services requires PSPs to comply with 'consumer and personal-data protection' rules, but neither source evidences dedicated payment-specific provisions on disclosure, liability allocation or dispute resolution. Recommend human review of the full Instruction text for a dedicated consumer-protection chapter before any upgrade to Yes.

Comments: BCEAO’s payment-systems management mandate includes compiling and releasing regular reports for WAEMU payment systems (SICA‑UEMOA/STAR‑UEMOA), implying at least annual public reporting via BCEAO publications/annual reports, but frequency for Togo-specific public KPIs not evidenced as quarterly/monthly in sources reviewed.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a much stronger source. BCEAO publishes a named 'Rapport annuel sur les systèmes de paiement' and a companion annual report on digital financial services in the UEMOA, each with detailed statistical annexes (e.g. the 2022-2023 IMF/payments report). No evidence of monthly/quarterly public bulletins was found, so Annual (3) is confirmed rather than upgraded.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: World Bank report (citing 2021 Global Findex) notes 57% of urban adults in Togo reported making a digital payment, indicating digital payment usage around the 50–69% band (at least in urban population).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed but flagged for review: the cited World Bank figure of 57% is for urban adults only, not the national adult population the variable requires; the World Bank's own 2019/20 Digital Economy Diagnostic put national digital-payment use at roughly a third of adults on earlier (2017) Findex data. A 2024 BCEAO-sourced figure (via Togo First) shows 6.07m active mobile-money accounts (likely including duplicate/multiple accounts per person) and a secondary aggregator (FinStatGlobe, lower authority) cites 53.1% digital-payment adoption for 2024, both broadly consistent with the 50-69% band, so the code is retained at 3, but the exact national Global Findex figure could not be independently verified without a microdata login — recommend human review.
